places.name: Shibuya Scramble Crossing
places.description: The world's busiest pedestrian crossing: 3,000 people cross simultaneously on every green light. Surrounded by giant LED screens, brands and department stores. Visible from Scramble Square sky deck.
highlights: Best viewed from Scramble Square 230m up

places.name: Meiji Jingu
places.description: Shinto shrine dedicated to Emperor Meiji and Empress Shoken, built in 1920. 70 hectares of forest at the heart of the city. 100,000 visitors on New Year's Day.

places.name: teamLab Planets
places.description: Immersive digital art museum in Toyosu. Wade through knee-deep water into infinity mirror rooms filled with floating flowers and koi fish. A 10,000m² world of light and reflection.

places.name: Tsukiji Outer Market
places.description: The surviving outer market of historic Tsukiji Fish Market. Tamagoyaki egg shops, fresh tuna rice bowls, oysters, street skewers. Open from 5am for an authentic Tokyo morning.
highlights: Freshest tuna don in Tokyo at 6am
Tamagoyaki — sweet rolled omelette on a stick

places.name: Harajuku Takeshita Street
places.description: Pedestrian street that invented Tokyo street fashion. Rainbow crepes, fairy kei, Lolita, and decora culture. Densest concentration of youth fashion in the world on a Saturday afternoon.
highlights: Marion Crêpes — longest queue, best crepe

places.name: Shinjuku Golden Gai
places.description: 200 tiny bars in a maze of alleys from the 1940s. Six lanes, 290 bars, each seating 5-8 people. Each bar has a unique theme: jazz, manga, cinema, classic rock. Unmistakably Tokyo.
highlights: Smallest bars in the world — 5 stools max
Each bar a curated universe of one theme

places.name: Shibuya Sky — Scramble Square
places.description: Open-air rooftop observation deck at 229m, atop Shibuya's tallest building. Unobstructed 360° views of Tokyo. Glass-edged walking platform, wind tunnel experience, Fuji-visible days.
highlights: Mt Fuji visible on clear days

places.name: Narisawa
places.description: Chef Yoshihiro Narisawa's two-Michelin-star restaurant, regularly in the World's 50 Best. Innovative satoyama cuisine: Japan's mountains and forests reimagined on the plate.
highlights: Bread baked at the table in a stone oven
Course inspired by Japan's four ecosystems
